rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2 Method <U+2013> semi-structured interviews with 82 farmers and managers of 5 WUAs in three collective systems (summers 2011<U+2013>2012), plus WUA internal documents and field observations. Q2: Section 4.2 'Changes in operating rules' <U+2013> new rules implemented to distribute water among farmers after drip: Vall d'Uix<U+00F3> WUA sets a maximum daily water use with valves automatically closed above it; a JTC WUA sets a volume limit above which price is higher; ARJ sets a flow-rate limit per plot with technical guidelines checked before admission; Section 4.1 <U+2013> WUAs now settle irrigation schedules by area and crop; Section 5.1 <U+2013> drip triggered merging of 19 GUAs into 12 in Vall d'Uix<U+00F3>, share-ceding rules in JTC, centralization of sector management in ARJ. Q5: results reported separately for the three districts (ARJ, JTC, Vall d'Uix<U+00F3>; Table 1, Sections 4.2 and 5.1), which differ in water source (surface, mixed, groundwater), size and institutional history. Q6: Table 1 and Sections 4<U+2013>5 <U+2013> effects reported at WUA/irrigation-district scale (2,395<U+2013>19,437 ha, thousands of members). Q7: Section 4.1 and Section 6 <U+2013> authors state that where a high level of automation and remote control exists, decision-making is concentrated in the WUA central offices, whereas in non-automatic systems farmers keep scheduling decisions; Section 3.3 <U+2013> a high share of unconnected farmers would create management problems, hence compulsory connection rules.
rows.notes: Q3 'no': farmer and manager interviews are one method; internal documents and field observations are mentioned only as contextual information and are not shown to independently establish the rule changes. Q4 'no': automation as the mechanism for centralization is described qualitatively from interviews, not measured. Q5 'yes' is borderline: the three districts are distinct irrigation schemes with separate results, but all lie within the Valencia region under one climate. No explicit limitations of sample or method (Q8) and no dispersion measures (Q9).

rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2 Method <U+2013> own interview survey of 82 farmers (70 with drip) and managers of 5 WUAs. Q2: Section 3.2 <U+2013> first reason for adopting drip was WUA obligation (50%), then increased production (16%); only 9% mentioned water saving; secondary reasons were product quality, convenience, economic and labour savings; Section 4.2 <U+2013> managers report some sectors using the same water as before drip, extra water supplied on demand, 'psychological irrigation' beyond crop needs; Section 4.3 <U+2013> duplicity of drip and furrow irrigation; Section 6 <U+2013> when these operating procedures are applied the water-saving potential of drip vanishes, and water saving goals become blurred along the top-down chain. Q6: Sections 4.2<U+2013>4.3 and 6 <U+2013> practices undermining water saving reported at WUA/sector scale across three irrigation districts. Q7: Section 6 <U+2013> authors state that water-saving potential vanishes when farmers/managers apply the described operating procedures (over-watering on demand, maintaining gravity networks, extra fertilizer), and Section 4.2 <U+2013> managers acknowledge they will need to restrict demand to realize savings, i.e. conservation requires WUA enforcement of allocations.
rows.notes: Q3 'no': farmer and manager interviews are the same method; no water-use measurements corroborate the reported practices. Q4 'no': the pathways (over-irrigation, complementary gravity irrigation) are described from interview statements, not measured. Q5 'no': motivation percentages are pooled across the 70 drip farmers, not reported per district. Q6 'yes' rests on manager statements about sectors, not measured volumes. No stated limitations of the sample or interview approach (Q8) and no dispersion statistics for the percentages (Q9).

notes: Full text appears complete. Qualitative/survey study (interviews in three Valencian collective irrigation systems); no quantitative water-use data of its own, so claims about actual water conservation rest on interviewee reports.
